question: Will the DFB formally and institutionally come out against Infantino's FIFA presidency before October 16, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of Oct 1-5 2026 (SRF, time.news): DFB has refused to sign Infantino's support letter but has not issued a formal organisational non-support/no-confidence statement; strong anti-Infantino remarks by Neuendorf and Watzke are personal and excluded. The UEFA meeting in Berlin on Oct 8-9 was flagged by Neuendorf as the decisive moment, and the DFB issued a qualifying-style institutional dfb.de statement before the 2023 Kigali election, so a statement inside the window is plausible. Against that: only 11 days remain, no Präsidium date was found, the DFB says it never endorsed him so there is nothing to withdraw, and coordinated action may come through UEFA or by backing a challenger later (nominations close Nov 18). Market check: no matching market; Polymarket has only an 'Infantino out by Dec 31 2026' market, a different event.
calls.dossier:
- SRF (2026-10-01): at least 50 associations worldwide oppose Infantino's re-election (Nordics, Belgium, Austria, England, France, Netherlands, Italy, USA, Canada, etc.); 'Germany has also not formally withdrawn support', but the DFB refused to sign the support letter.
- time.news (2026-10-05): Swiss FA (SFV) formally withdrew its endorsement; European leaders met at the Ritz-Carlton Berlin; DFB attendees were Neuendorf, GS Holger Blask and VP Watzke (UEFA ExCo member); DFB 'has not formally withdrawn support'; the 55 UEFA associations are examining prospective candidates through late October.
- Sportschau (2026-09-15): Neuendorf said 'Das Vertrauensverhältnis zu Gianni Infantino, zu dieser FIFA-Führung ist natürlich zerrüttet' and that the 'System Infantino' must end; he named the UEFA meeting in Berlin on Oct 8-9 as the moment for important decisions; he wants an 'integre Persönlichkeit' as a candidate. Ten European FAs had formally withdrawn support by then.
- Sport1 (Sept 2026): Watzke said Infantino 'sollte weg, ohne Wenn und Aber' after the UEFA ExCo in Thessaloniki (personal remark, excluded by the fine print).
- July 2026 (zdfheute/sport1): DFB did not sign the support letter circulated by FIFA's Elkhan Mammadov; further steps to be discussed in the DFB Präsidium.
- Precedent: dfb.de news (2023-03-15), 'Neuendorf: DFB unterstützt Wiederwahl von Infantino nicht', framed as an organisational position ('Der DFB wird die Wiederwahl ... in Kigali nicht unterstützen'). It refers to the 2023 congress, so it does not qualify for March 2027, but it shows the DFB has used the qualifying wording before.
- Status quo outcome: no formal DFB organisational statement taking position (a)/(b)/(c); DFB's line has been that it never endorsed Infantino.
- Resolves off an official DFB statement (dfb.de press release/news, Präsidium resolution) or credible reporting characterising it as the DFB organisational position, not off personal remarks by Neuendorf/Watzke, mere non-signing, or a UEFA joint statement.
- Event window: any time up to before 2026-10-16 (earlier statements count, but none found for the 2027 election); as of 2026-10-05 about 11 days remain.
- Rival nominations deadline is 2026-11-18; Congress 2027-03-18 in Rabat. European coordination may run through a UEFA-backed candidate rather than individual FA statements.
- Markets: no market on this specific question found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi); only an unrelated 'Infantino out by Dec 31' Polymarket market exists.
- Searched, absent: a scheduled DFB Präsidium meeting date in October 2026; any post-Oct-5 DFB statement; any outcome of the Oct 8-9 Berlin meeting.
calls.reference_class: European FAs strongly critical of Infantino that convert rhetoric into a formal organisational non-support statement within a ~2-week window around a key coordination meeting

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no organisation-level DFB statement. As of Oct 1–5 reports say the DFB 'has not yet formally withdrawn support'. Its only institutional act was refusing to sign the support letter, with further steps referred to the Präsidium. That refusal is excluded by the fine print. Base rate: ~10 European FAs formally withdrew within ~2 months, which suggests a meaningful hazard. But the DFB has held back for months despite harsh personal remarks from Neuendorf, Watzke and Blask, possibly because Neuendorf sits on the FIFA Council. Catalysts inside the 11-day window: the UEFA summit in Berlin Oct 8–9 (rival candidate expected) and the FIFA Council on Oct 15. A post-Berlin Präsidium decision or a DFB statement backing a rival could qualify; joint UEFA statements or more personal quotes would not. No matching market found; Polymarket's 'Infantino out by Dec 31' market is not comparable.
calls.dossier:
- Jul 2026 (zdfheute, sport1): DFB did not sign the FIFA-circulated letter of support for Infantino's re-election; a DFB statement said further steps would be discussed in the DFB Präsidium. Under the fine print this refusal alone does not count.
- Sep 9 2026 (ligaportal): Neuendorf said FIFA must be fundamentally reformed and that 'further waymarks' would be set at the Sep 15 UEFA ExCo/FIFA Council in Thessaloniki and the Oct 8-9 Berlin meeting of all 55 UEFA association presidents and general secretaries.
- Sep 2026 (t-online, sportschau): Neuendorf called Infantino's reform letter a 'transparent maneuver', said he 'has lost all credibility' and that the 'Infantino system' must end. DFB general secretary Blask said he 'personally' cannot see how Infantino could restore the DFB's trust. All of these are personal attributions.
- Sep 18 2026 (Al Jazeera): VP Watzke said Infantino 'must go, no ifs or buts'. Personal remark.
- Oct 1 2026 (SRF): list of associations that turned away from Infantino (Nordics, Belgium, Austria, England, France, Netherlands, Italy, Switzerland, USA, Canada...). Germany is described only as refusing to sign the support letter, not as formally withdrawing.
- Oct 2-5 2026 (footy.de, time.news): UEFA plans to settle a counter-candidate/strategy at the Berlin summit Oct 8-9 (Ritz-Carlton). DFB attends with Neuendorf, Blask and Watzke. Time.news (Oct 5): the DFB 'has not yet formally withdrawn support'.
- Upcoming: FIFA Council in Zurich Oct 15. Nomination deadline Nov 18. Congress Mar 18 2027 in Rabat.
- Base rate: about 10 European FAs formally withdrew support between Aug and early Oct 2026 (roughly 2 months), e.g. KNVB on Aug 1/Aug 30, France, Austria, Switzerland. The DFB has held back for months despite the harshest rhetoric; Neuendorf sits on the FIFA Council.
- Status quo: no qualifying DFB organisational statement exists.
- Resolves off an official DFB organisational statement (dfb.de press release / Präsidium resolution, or credible reports characterising it as the DFB's official position). Not off personal interviews, joint UEFA statements, or non-signature alone.
- Event window: any time before Oct 16 2026 (earlier statements count, but none is found to date). Now = Oct 5; about 11 days remain, and the Berlin summit falls inside the window.
- Searched but not found: a scheduled date for a DFB Präsidium meeting in October; any dfb.de news item on a formal position; a human market on this specific question (only Polymarket's 'Infantino out by Dec 31' exists, which is not comparable).

calls.reasoning: Status quo is NO: as of Oct 1-5, 2026, multiple outlets say the DFB has not formally withdrawn support. Its only institutional act, not signing FIFA's letter of support, is excluded by the fine print. Neuendorf's strong personal remarks (trust 'shattered', the 'Infantino system' must end) do not count unless framed as an official DFB position. The main catalyst inside the 11-day window is the UEFA members' meeting in Berlin on Oct 8-9, where Sportschau reported key decisions would be made at the latest, with a DFB Präsidium deliberation expected afterwards. Against this: the DFB has preferred to coordinate within UEFA, UEFA reportedly weighs candidates through late October, and no Präsidium date inside the window was found. Strong peer momentum (~10 European associations already withdrawn) keeps a YES quite possible. calls.dossier:
- July 2026 (ZDFheute, Sport1): the DFB confirmed it did not sign FIFA's letter of support for Infantino's re-election; further steps were to be discussed in the DFB Präsidium. More than 200 associations reportedly signed.
- Sep 15, 2026 (Sportschau/Tagesspiegel/dpa): Neuendorf said the relationship of trust with Infantino and the FIFA leadership is 'zerrüttet' (shattered) and that it is 'important that the Infantino system ends'; he called a leadership change 'absolutely necessary'. These were personal remarks; the articles say the DFB had not formally withdrawn support, unlike ~10 European FAs (most recently France and Austria).
- Sportschau Sep 15: important decisions to come 'at the latest in Berlin' when all UEFA member associations meet Oct 8-9.
- Oct 1, 2026 (SRF): at least ~50 federations oppose Infantino (Nordics, Belgium, Austria, England, France, Netherlands, Italy, Switzerland, USA, Canada, Caribbean nations, New Zealand); Germany is listed as not having formally withdrawn, only as having refused to sign the letter.
- Oct 5, 2026 (time.news): Neuendorf, general secretary Blask and Watzke are attending the Berlin UEFA summit; 'the DFB has not yet formally withdrawn support'; UEFA's 55 members are reportedly examining prospective candidates through late October. Swiss FA (SFV) withdrew support.
- The FIFA nomination deadline is Nov 18, 2026; the Congress is Mar 18, 2027 in Rabat. UEFA is reportedly considering legal steps and wants to field a challenger.
- A possible reason for DFB restraint: it says it never endorsed Infantino, so there is nothing to 'withdraw'; it prefers coordinated UEFA action; Neuendorf sits on the FIFA Council.
- Status quo: no qualifying institutional DFB statement as of Oct 5.
- Resolution: resolves off an official DFB organisational statement (dfb.de news, press release, Präsidium resolution) explicitly taking positions (a), (b) or (c); not off personal interviews by Neuendorf or Watzke, and not off non-signature.
- Event window: any time before Oct 16, 2026 -> Oct 16, 2026 00:00 UTC (earlier qualifying statements count; none found). As of Oct 5, 07:20 UTC, about 11 days remain, with the Berlin meeting (Oct 8-9) inside the window.

calls.reasoning: Status quo is NO: as of Oct 1-5, 2026 reporting says the DFB has not formally withdrawn support. Its only institutional act, refusing to sign the support letter, is excluded by the fine print, and the leaders' strong quotes are personal. The main catalyst inside the window is the UEFA summit in Berlin on Oct 8-9, which Neuendorf named as the moment for decisions, possibly followed by a Präsidium resolution. The DFB published exactly this kind of 'DFB will not support re-election' statement on dfb.de in 2023. Against that: only 11 days remain, no Präsidium date is known, UEFA's candidate assessment runs until late October with nominations open until Nov 18, and the DFB's line is that it never endorsed Infantino.
calls.reconciliation: No factual disputes: all runs agree that no qualifying DFB statement exists as of Oct 5, that a Präsidium date is unknown, and that the Berlin summit on Oct 8-9 falls inside the window. The spread from 0.22 to 0.30 is judgment about whether the DFB acts in the window or waits for UEFA's candidate process, which runs until late October. Two points push slightly upward: the 2023 dfb.de precedent with near-qualifying wording, and the looser 'credible reporting characterises as DFB position' clause. Two points push downward: the DFB's 'nothing to withdraw' line and Neuendorf's FIFA Council seat. I took 0.27. No web retrieval on this run.
